decisions.executionNote: Begin gradual elbow-up approaches with open grippers; left toward purple nut, right toward blue nut. Geometry estimated from current calibrated head view.
Complete downward tool orientation while staying elbow-up, then center over purple and blue nuts at clearance height.
Correct lateral alignment using wrist views and descend slowly to nut grasp height; leave grippers open for visual confirmation.
Close both grippers fully, lift to verify retention, and begin separated paths toward central nut staging locations.
Both nuts appear retained. Move purple toward the left side of central staging and blue toward the near central staging point, keeping their paths separated.
Set blue nut upright at the near center and release, withdrawing the right arm. Bring purple to a separated far-center staging point and lower while holding.
Corrected malformed final row; no prior motion executed. Release purple, separate arms, and approach staged nuts for the opposite arms.
Use smaller initial retraction increments after continuity rejection near far-center reach. Right rotates in place, waiting for left to clear.
Approach the released central blue nut with left and far purple nut with right on separated near/far paths; descend cautiously before confirming alignment.
Tracking suggests interference near center. Separate left toward the near side and right toward the far side before resuming nut acquisition, using smaller steps.
Align over the staged nuts on separated near/far center positions; right remains at the workspace boundary. Slow descent for visual confirmation before closure.
Left closes around staged blue and lifts for retention check. Right retracts from reach limit while tilting the tool toward purple, then cautiously lowers.
No previous motion executed. Reduce right retraction/tilt to quarter-size initial increments to preserve joint continuity; left aligns, closes and lifts blue.
Carry visibly retained blue nut above its left-side bolt. Lower and make a small visual alignment correction toward the purple nut with right.
Lower the centered blue nut to engage its bolt with a small upright correction. Make a small right-hand lateral correction over the staged purple nut before closing.
Fine-center blue on the bolt and begin a slow clockwise tightening stroke. Center and close on purple, then lift slightly to check retention.
Continue blue clockwise stroke with a small image-based centering correction. Carry retained purple toward its matching bolt while restoring vertical orientation.
Release blue briefly and reset wrist for another tightening stroke without backing the nut off. Bring purple into alignment above its bolt at insertion height.
Blue tipped after release, so withdraw for recovery rather than assume fastening. Correct purple's visible off-center bolt and try a slow clockwise engagement stroke.
Lift purple out of uncertain engagement and restore the grasp-time tilt so the nut itself is upright; compensate its offset from link6 before reinsertion.
Purple bolt is visible through the nut; lower slowly with the recovered nut orientation, without turning yet, to test coaxial engagement.
Turn purple clockwise with a small helical descent and compensate the tilted tool's horizontal offset, aiming to keep the nut over the bolt.
Pause turning and correct purple's lateral displacement from the tilted link6 offset; reseat slowly while keeping the grasp closed.
Purple now appears better centered. Release and lift clear to verify it remains upright, then start resetting the wrist for a vertical regrasp.
Purple remains on its bolt after release. Straighten the tool above its visible center and reset yaw, descending with the gripper open for an upright regrasp.
Purple is still visibly tilted, so avoid claiming fastening. Clear both partial pairs and approach the untouched yellow nut for a clean, upright transfer.
Descend vertically toward the upright yellow nut with a small fore-aft correction, keeping the gripper open until close-range alignment is visible.
Close on yellow at low grasp height, lift while keeping its upright orientation, and start a near-center transfer clear of the left arm.
Carry the visibly retained yellow nut upright to near-center staging, with the left arm waiting clear.
Yellow is no longer visible between the fingers. Clear the right arm upward and rightward to locate the dropped nut before any further placement attempt.
Yellow nut is located near right-center. Approach it for recovery while left approaches the yellow bolt; avoid the other two pairs.
Lower to recover the yellow nut and grasp the yellow bolt shaft with left after a small visual centering correction. Verify both before transfer.
Lift both yellow parts to verify retention. Bring the bolt toward near-center staging while holding the nut safely on the right.
Yellow bolt was not retained, so leave it on the table. Carry the retained yellow nut more slowly toward near-center staging and clear the left arm.
Slowly lower the retained yellow nut at near-center staging, keeping the arms separated and checking its tilted placement before release.
Set yellow down gently and release so it can settle; retract right before bringing left toward the staged nut.
Inspect the staged yellow nut closely with left while moving right fully clear. It appears to have settled on a side, so reorientation may be needed.
Grasp the side-set yellow nut for reorientation. Reapproach purple's seated pair upright to inspect and resume tightening if aligned.
Lift and begin rolling the side-grasped yellow nut upright. Close around the visibly seated purple nut and apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke.
Finish the purple tightening stroke and release for a wrist reset. Continue rolling the side-held yellow nut toward upright while bringing it over its matching bolt.
Corrected the malformed rotation row; the rejected tensor moved nothing. Lower yellow with fixed orientation and reset purple yaw only after opening.
Continue a clockwise purple tightening pass with gentle downward tracking. Lower the side-held, reoriented yellow nut toward its bolt without further wrist rotation.
Release yellow near its bolt and retract to inspect its settled alignment rather than force through contact. Finish the purple stroke, open, and partially reset the wrist.
Return the empty left tool toward a downward orientation above the table. Regrasp purple after completing the open reset and apply another controlled clockwise stroke.
Finish another purple turn and begin an open-gripper reset. Blue now appears upright on its bolt; approach it with left for a centered vertical regrasp.
Fine-align and close on the upright blue nut, then turn clockwise. Complete purple's open reset, regrasp, and continue its tightening.
Continue both aligned nuts clockwise with small downward tracking, then release and start an open reset without reversing the nuts.
Corrected an erroneous right-wrist entry; rejected commands executed nothing. Lift the open right gripper clear of purple and reset/regrasp blue for another tightening stroke.
Finish blue's tightening stroke and release. Purple remains upright after withdrawal; move the right arm back within its workspace while resetting its orientation.
Corrected row 18; no prior motion executed. Approach upright yellow with left while returning the empty right arm gradually toward origin.
Descend squarely onto the upright yellow nut with a small calibrated lateral correction, gripper open. Complete the gradual right-arm return toward origin.
Center yellow between the fingers, close fully, and lift vertically to verify retention and upright alignment. Leave the right arm open at origin.
Yellow is retained upright. Lift for clearance and translate over its matching bolt, preserving the grasp orientation before descent.
Lower yellow slowly without turning, using the bolt's appearance through the nut to check final lateral alignment.
Correct the visible yellow bolt offset with a slow fore-aft translation, then lower a few millimeters for coaxial engagement before turning.
Yellow is horizontally centered in the wrist view but still offset along the other image axis. Apply a small diagonal correction with almost no descent before tightening.
Yellow's bolt is now visible through the centered hole. Apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke with a small downward feed, keeping the right arm parked open.
Release yellow briefly to let it seat, reset the wrist counterclockwise with fingers open, then regrasp without reversing the nut.
Continue yellow clockwise at low speed with gentle downward feed, maintaining the centered grasp and leaving the right arm parked open.
Open and reset the left wrist without unscrewing yellow, then regrasp for another tightening pass. Correct the small right-arm origin drift.
Continue the seated yellow nut clockwise through another short tightening stroke with a gentle downward feed.
Reset the open left wrist through a wider arc, leaving yellow on its bolt, and close again for the next tightening stroke.
Tighten yellow clockwise through two radians with a small downward feed, watching for seating rather than relying on gripper state.
Release yellow and lift clear to inspect its settled alignment and depth, resetting yaw only with the gripper open.
Yellow remains upright on its bolt after release. Regrasp the settled nut vertically for a final tightening pass rather than turn an uncertain suspended grasp.
Apply another controlled clockwise yellow tightening stroke with four millimeters of downward tracking; right stays open at origin.
Release yellow and lift clear to inspect all three pairs. Reset the empty left wrist above the table before returning toward origin.
All three pairs remain together after release. Begin a gradual open-gripper return of the left arm toward origin, preserving configuration continuity.
Complete the gradual left-arm return to origin with both grippers open, leaving the three color-matched pairs undisturbed.
Settle both open arms precisely at origin and observe whether the three assembled pairs remain stable.
Yellow still shows more exposed internal thread than the other pairs. Reapproach it gradually with the left arm for a closer depth check, keeping the right arm parked.
Finish the downward approach over yellow with open fingers, preserving elbow-up continuity and checking the settled nut before any further turn.
Center the gripper on yellow's settled nut, close at the lower height, and begin a slow clockwise pass with small downward tracking.
Continue yellow's clockwise turn with a small additional depth feed, then release and begin an open reset to inspect seating.
Reset with fingers open, regrasp the seated yellow nut, and begin one more short tightening pass to improve its visible depth.
Complete the yellow clockwise tightening stroke with a small downward feed, staying within the current wrist configuration.
Release and slightly lift from yellow, then reset the open wrist to inspect the settled nut and improve grasp centering if needed.
Regrasp yellow at its settled height with the centered, upright tool, and begin another slow clockwise engagement stroke.
Complete a short clockwise yellow stroke with less than three millimeters of downward feed, stopping before the wrist limit.
